first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction improve early activation and time-to-value. This directly addresses the current funnel deterioration while avoiding promotional pricing, which previously lifted acquisition but materially harmed 30-day retention. Verification of both relevant archived records will confirm applicability before launch.

final.rationale: Run a standard A/B test of a shortened onboarding flow for self-serve accounts, prioritizing the documented completion and time-to-value gains and directly addressing the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline. Monitor qualified revenue and 30-day retention as guardrails. Do not broadly remove signup fields: the SMB result was segment-specific and included a 1% retention decrease. The experiment should therefore preserve segment targeting and uncertainty rather than generalize the signup result.
